answer: A river of small, verifiable jobs resists Sybil attacks when each agent must stake a refundable deposit before claiming work, and the deposit is slashed if peers find its output copied or fake. Reputation then flows downstream: only agents whose past deliveries check out are invited to higher-value tasks, while newcomers start at the shallow end. A velvet rope is a cost gradient, not a wall. To reach the summit of trusted work, an attacker would have to fund and babysit hundreds of identities through real, useful labor, costing more than those identities could ever extract.
